name: Electric Scooters
hub_intro: Electric scooters became fully legal on Irish public roads in May 2024 — and sales have exploded since. To be road-legal in Ireland your e-scooter must be limited to 25 km/h, weigh under 25 kg and have a max continuous power of 400 W (motors are rated at continuous power; check compliance before buying). We compare the models that actually make sense for Irish roads, weather and law.
guide: To ride legally on public roads: max 25 km/h, max 25 kg, no passengers, riders must be 16+. No tax, insurance or licence needed. Models sold as 'road legal Ireland' are configured for these limits — always confirm before buying.

Manufacturers test range at low speed with a light rider on flat ground. In real Irish conditions — hills, wind, rain, a 75–90 kg rider — expect roughly 60–70% of the claimed figure. If you commute 10 km each way, buy at least 30 km of claimed range.
This is Ireland. Look for an IP54 rating or better. IPX4 handles light rain; anything unrated will eventually die on a wet commute and most warranties exclude water damage.
Pneumatic (air) tyres grip far better on wet Irish roads than solid tyres and absorb potholes. Dual braking (disc + electronic) is worth paying for — wet braking distances roughly double.

faqs.q: Are electric scooters legal in Ireland?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 20 May 2024, e-scooters meeting the rules (max 25 km/h, under 25 kg, 16+ rider, no passengers) are legal on public roads without tax, insurance or a licence. They are banned from motorways and footpaths.

faqs.q: Do I need insurance or a licence for an e-scooter in Ireland?
faqs.a: No. Compliant e-scooters don't require insurance, road tax or a driving licence in Ireland. You must be at least 16 years old, and Gardaí can seize non-compliant scooters.

faqs.q: Can I ride an electric scooter in the rain in Ireland?
faqs.a: With an IP54+ rated scooter, yes — light to moderate rain is fine. Avoid deep puddles, dry the scooter after wet rides, and never jet-wash it. Water damage usually isn't covered by warranty.

faqs.q: What range do I really need for commuting?
faqs.a: Take your daily round trip and double it — that's the claimed range you should buy. Real-world range is typically 60–70% of the brochure figure once you factor in hills, wind, rider weight and cold batteries.

faqs.q: Are cheap electric scooters worth it?
faqs.a: Under €300 you generally get weak brakes, solid tyres and short battery life. The €400–600 bracket is the sweet spot in Ireland — proper braking, air tyres and batteries that last 2–3 years of commuting.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to charge an e-scooter in Ireland?
faqs.a: Almost nothing. A typical 360 Wh battery costs roughly 13–15 cents to fully charge at standard Irish electricity rates — a few euro per year for most commuters, versus €100+ monthly on bus or Luas fares.

faqs.q: Can heavier riders use electric scooters?
faqs.a: Yes, but check the max load rating. Many budget scooters cap at 100 kg and performance drops near the limit. Riders over 95 kg should choose models rated 120 kg with 500 W+ motors for hills.

faqs.q: Where can I not ride an e-scooter in Ireland?
faqs.a: Footpaths, pedestrianised zones and motorways are off-limits. Use cycle lanes where available. Local authorities can add restrictions, so check council bye-laws — and helmets, while not mandatory, are strongly recommended.

pages.title: 5 Best Electric Scooters in Ireland 2026 (Road-Legal, Tested Picks)
pages.desc: We compared Ireland's best road-legal electric scooters for 2026 — range, hills, rain-readiness and value. See our top 5 picks with full specs and prices.
pages.h1: The 5 Best Electric Scooters in Ireland (2026)
pages.intro: E-scooters have been street-legal in Ireland since May 2024, and the market has been flooded — including plenty of models that don't meet Irish rules or survive Irish weather. We filtered down to five road-legal scooters that handle wet roads, real hills and daily commuting, then compared range, brakes, tyres and total value so you can pick in five minutes.

products.name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 4 Pro (2nd Gen)
pros: Huge real-world range (≈40 km) for the price
Self-sealing air tyres handle Irish potholes
cons: 17 kg is heavy to carry upstairs
Folding latch feels less premium than rivals
products.verdict: The best all-rounder you can buy in Ireland right now: legal limits out of the box, class-leading range, and tyres and water sealing built for our roads and weather.

products.name: Segway Ninebot MAX G2 E
pros: Front + rear suspension irons out bad roads
cons: 21 kg — awkward on stairs and buses
Pricier than the Xiaomi for similar range
products.verdict: The tank of commuter scooters. If your route includes rough surfaces or steady hills, the G2's suspension and torque justify the extra €100 over our top pick.

products.name: Aovo Pro AP07
pros: Turn signals included — rare at this price
cons: Real range closer to 22–25 km
8.5" tyres feel potholes more than 10" rivals
products.verdict: The smart budget pick: road-legal, rain-rated and equipped with indicators most €600 scooters lack. Ideal for commutes under 10 km each way.

products.name: Pure Advance Flex
pros: Unique forward-facing riding stance — far more stable
IP65: the most waterproof scooter here
Folds smaller than anything in its class
cons: Premium price for mid-pack range
Riding position takes a day to get used to
products.verdict: Designed in the UK for exactly this climate. The side-by-side stance transforms stability on wet roads, and IP65 sealing makes it the true all-weather choice.

products.name: Ninebot KickScooter F2 E
cons: No suspension — tyres do all the work
Display washes out in bright sun
products.verdict: The sensible middle: Segway reliability, proper range and traction control at a price between budget and premium. The default choice for daily Dublin commuting.

pages.title: Best Electric Scooters Under €500 in Ireland (2026) — Top 5 Compared
pages.desc: Five road-legal electric scooters under €500 that don't cut corners on brakes, tyres or rain protection. Compared for Irish commuters on a budget.
pages.h1: Best Electric Scooters Under €500 in Ireland
pages.intro: Under €500 is where most Irish buyers shop — and where most of the junk lives. The trick is knowing which corners manufacturers cut: solid tyres that slide on wet tarmac, single brakes, no water rating. These five models keep the safety-critical features and trim the luxuries instead, so you get a legal, rain-ready commuter without crossing the €500 line.

products.name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 4 Lite (2nd Gen)
cons: Real range ~17 km — short commutes only
Struggles on steeper hills
products.verdict: The safest sub-€350 buy in Ireland. You give up range, not safety: full-size air tyres, proper braking and Xiaomi's parts availability.

products.name: Aovo Pro M365 Upgraded
pros: Claimed 35 km — best range claim under €350
cons: Brakes need adjustment out of the box
Build quality is functional, not premium
products.verdict: Maximum kilometres per euro. Treat the first 30 minutes as setup time (check brakes, tyre pressure) and it'll serve a 6–8 km commute faithfully.

products.name: Segway Ninebot E2 Pro E
pros: Segway quality control at budget price
cons: 9" tyres middle ground, not great on potholes
App locked to one phone at a time
products.verdict: Boringly dependable — exactly what you want at this price. The drum brake needs near-zero maintenance, ideal for riders who'll never touch an Allen key.

products.name: iScooter i9 Max
cons: Solid tyres grip less in heavy rain
Real range nearer 18 km
products.verdict: The floor of acceptable quality. The honeycomb tyres trade wet grip for zero punctures — a fair deal if you ride mostly on dry days and good surfaces.

products.name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 4 (Standard)
pros: Self-sealing tyres fix small punctures alone
cons: €449 is the very top of 'budget'
No suspension
products.verdict: Spend the extra €100 over entry models and you get the feature that matters most on Irish roads: self-sealing 10-inch air tyres. The best sub-€500 scooter, full stop.

pages.title: Best Long-Range Electric Scooters Ireland 2026 — 5 Premium Picks
pages.desc: Need 40+ km of real range? We compared Ireland's best premium long-range e-scooters on battery, comfort and build. Top 5 ranked for 2026.
pages.h1: Best Long-Range & Premium Electric Scooters in Ireland
pages.intro: If your commute is 15 km+ each way, or you simply hate charging every night, you need a genuine 40+ km of real-world range — which means a claimed range of 60 km and up. These five premium machines deliver big batteries plus the comfort features (suspension, wide decks, bigger tyres) that long rides demand. All remain within Irish legal limits.

products.name: Segway Ninebot MAX G3 E
pros: Real-world 55+ km range — a full week of commutes
cons: 24 kg, right at the legal weight limit
Serious money for a scooter
products.verdict: The best scooter money can legally buy in Ireland. A week of 10 km commutes on one charge, with suspension that makes rural roads feel resurfaced.

products.name: Pure Advance+
pros: IP65 — highest water rating on the market
Indicators, brake light, unique stable stance
7 kg lighter than the MAX G3
cons: Range trails the Segway by ~15 km
Distinct stance isn't for everyone
products.verdict: Built for the worst of Irish weather. If you'll ride through winter rain five days a week, the sealing and visibility features beat raw range.

products.name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 5 Max
pros: 60 km claimed for €250 less than rivals
cons: App nags about region settings
Charger is slow (6+ hours)
products.verdict: Eighty percent of the MAX G3 experience for 75% of the price. The rational long-range choice if you charge overnight anyway.

products.name: NIU KQi3 Max
pros: Dual disc brakes — shortest stops in test
Wide deck and bars feel planted
cons: No suspension at all
Heavy without the comfort payoff
products.verdict: The braking benchmark. On wet descents, the KQi3 Max stops metres shorter than anything here — worth the comfort trade-off in hilly towns like Cork.

products.name: VMAX VX2 Pro GT
pros: Monster peak torque for steep hills
Real 45+ km range with heavy rider
cons: Brand less known in Ireland — fewer parts
23 kg near the legal cap
products.verdict: The strongest climber under the Irish power rules. If your route includes the kind of hill that kills other scooters' momentum, this is your answer.

pages.title: Best Lightweight & Folding Electric Scooters Ireland 2026 (Under 15 kg)
pages.desc: Carrying your scooter on the Luas, DART or up office stairs? These 5 lightweight folding e-scooters under 15 kg are Ireland's best portable picks.
pages.h1: Best Lightweight & Folding Electric Scooters in Ireland
pages.intro: Mixed commuting — scooter to the DART, carry on board, scoot to the office — is the killer use case in Dublin, but only if your scooter weighs little enough to actually lift. Every pick here is under 15 kg, folds in seconds and still meets road rules. We weighted portability, fold mechanism quality and whether the range survives the weight diet.

products.name: Xiaomi Mi Electric Scooter 3 Lite
pros: Three-second fold, carries like a briefcase
cons: Real range ~14 km
Narrow deck for big feet
products.verdict: The proven formula: light, legal, air-tyred and affordable. Perfect for the last 3 km between station and office, less so for full commutes.

products.name: Segway Ninebot Air T15E
pros: Just 10.5 kg — lightest legal scooter around
cons: 12 km claimed range is genuinely tiny
Premium price for short legs
products.verdict: A design object that happens to scoot. Buy it for a sub-4 km hop you repeat daily with stairs involved; buy anything else for longer rides.

products.name: Pure Air4
pros: IP65 waterproofing in a 15 kg body
Full 10" air tyres — unusual this light
cons: Right at our 15 kg ceiling
Fold latch is stiff when new
products.verdict: The portable pick that doesn't fear December. Best tyres and best sealing in the lightweight class make it the year-round choice.

products.name: iScooter i8
cons: Solid tyres + no suspension = firm ride
15 km realistic range
products.verdict: The cheapest scooter we'd still call good. For students or first-timers testing whether scooter commuting sticks, the entry fee is unbeatable.

products.name: ducati Pro-I Evo Safe Ride
pros: Turn signals on a 12.5 kg scooter
Tubeless tyres rare at this weight
Strong brand warranty support in EU
cons: Badge adds to price
App is basic
products.verdict: Indicators, tubeless tyres and a recognisable warranty network in a genuinely portable frame — the feature density winner of the lightweight class.

pages.title: Best Electric Scooters for Heavy Adults Ireland 2026 (120 kg+ Rated)
pages.desc: Top 5 electric scooters for riders over 95 kg in Ireland — high load ratings, strong motors for hills, wide decks. Compared and ranked for 2026.
pages.h1: Best Electric Scooters for Heavier Riders in Ireland
pages.intro: Most scooters are rated to 100 kg — and ride poorly long before that. For riders 95 kg and up, the wrong purchase means crawling up hills, halved range and early brake wear. These five models carry 118–150 kg ratings, torque that holds 25 km/h on inclines with a heavier rider, and frames built to take it. Ratings and realistic expectations below.

products.name: Segway Ninebot MAX G2 E (120 kg)
pros: Holds speed on hills with 110 kg aboard
Range stays ~35 km with heavy rider
cons: 21 kg to lug when not riding
Deck could be wider still
products.verdict: The complete package for bigger riders: honest 120 kg rating, torque that doesn't fade on inclines, and suspension that works with the load rather than bottoming out.

products.name: VMAX VX2 Pro ST
pros: 150 kg rating — highest of any legal scooter
Wide deck, tall bars suit riders over 1.9 m
cons: Fewer Irish service options
Heavy to carry
products.verdict: The only mainstream legal scooter rated to 150 kg. Tall or heavy riders finally get a machine sized for them instead of scaled up from a teenager's toy.

products.name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 5 Max (118 kg)
pros: Keeps ~38 km range with 100 kg rider
cons: 118 kg cap is tight for 110 kg+ riders with bags
Suspension is firm
products.verdict: For riders in the 95–110 kg band who still want range: the 5 Max loses less battery to body weight than anything we compared.

products.name: NIU KQi 300X
pros: Front + rear suspension rated for full load
cons: Range drops faster under load than Xiaomi
App setup mandatory before first ride
products.verdict: Comfort-first for bigger riders: the suspension keeps working at 115 kg where rivals turn rigid, and the wide deck ends foot-shuffling on long rides.

products.name: iScooter iX4
pros: Chunky tyres absorb kerbs and gravel
Peak power handles moderate hills loaded
cons: Build quality below the big brands
Realistic range ~25 km loaded
products.verdict: Proof that heavier riders don't need €700+. Hardware essentials — load rating, torque, big tyres — at almost half the price, if you accept plainer finish.
